To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the antioxidative function (i.e. protection against oxidative damage) of some thiols can be switched to a prooxidant function (i.e., enhancement of oxidative damage) by the presence of certain chelators in metal‐catalysed oxidation systems.
thiols can be either antioxidants or prooxidants, depending on the composition of the metal‐oxidant system.

the inactivation of glucose‐6‐ phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) by metal‐catabolyzed oxidation systems (Fe(II)/ H 2O 2/EDTA, Fe(II)/ADP) is mediated via the formation of superoxide and hydroxyl radicals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of thiols and metal ions in oxidative stress and in the pathogenesis of diseases.
the question of the role of metal‐catalysed oxidation systems in the inactivation of bovin glucose‐6‐ phosphate dehydrogenase and the role of thiols in this process.
the role of thiols in metal‐catalysed oxidation systems and the influence of the chelators on the antioxidative function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antioxidative function is a function of the chelators and not a property of the thiols.
the metal‐cated oxidation of thiols is not necessarily prooxidative.
thiols are prooxidants when the chelating capacity of the chelating agent is not sufficient to keep the metal in the reduced state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thiols studied are antioxidants against metal‐catalysed oxidation systems in the presence of ADP, whereas they are prooxidants in the presence of EDTA.
the antioxidative function is not restricted to a few specific molecules but that the whole thiol pool of the cell may be involved in the antioxidative defense.

the antioxidative function is shifted to a thiol‐dependent prooxidant activity of metal‐catalysed oxidation systems when the natural chelators of the enzyme are removed and replaced by a non‐natural chelator such as EDTA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metal‐catalysed oxidation systems can be used for the inactivation of proteins.
the nature of a chelator determines whether a thiol is acting as a prooxidant or as an antioxidant.
the antioxidative function and the prooxidative function of some thiol compounds are not mutually exclusive.
